classes.name: Levothyroxine (T4)
classes.description: Levothyroxine sodium: generic tablets and the brands Synthroid, Levoxyl, Unithroid, Euthyrox; Tirosint capsules; oral solutions Tirosint-SOL, Thyquidity, Ermeza. Generic tablets are AB-rated to specific reference brands, so a brand-only rule matters. Not liothyronine or desiccated thyroid.
classes.plainDescription: The standard daily pill that replaces thyroid hormone when your thyroid is underactive.

classes.name: Liothyronine (T3) and desiccated thyroid
classes.description: Liothyronine (Cytomel, generic tablets) and desiccated thyroid (Armour Thyroid, NP Thyroid; unapproved drugs under FDA enforcement action, often non-formulary; Adthyza reportedly discontinued). Levothyroxine is never this class's pick.
classes.plainDescription: Other thyroid pills, used alongside or instead of levothyroxine in some patients.

preferredAgent.sig: Healthy adults: full replacement about 1.6 mcg/kg once daily. Older adults or heart disease: start 12.5 to 25 mcg daily and raise by 12.5 to 25 mcg every 6 to 8 weeks. Adjust to TSH. Take on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast (label).
preferredAgent.sigShort: Start per weight/age, titrate to TSH
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill every morning on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Your dose is adjusted by blood tests.

records.tier: Covered (not a PDL class; Texas Medicaid formulary)
records.verificationNote: Not a PDL class: no thyroid heading in the PDL table of contents (p.6-9). Levothyroxine, Synthroid, Levoxyl, Unithroid, Euthyrox, Tirosint, Thyquidity and Ermeza do not appear in any of the 88 pages. No status inferred; PDL p.2 says it holds a subset. No BOGL flag because the PDL does not state a brand preference. Pick per brief.

preferredAgent.sig: Start 25 mcg by mouth once daily; increase by 25 mcg every 1 to 2 weeks to the usual 25 to 75 mcg daily. Start 5 mcg daily in older adults or with heart disease (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill a day; your dose is adjusted by symptoms and blood tests.

records.verificationNote: Read from the formulary text layer, row by row (each tier digit sits on the same row as its drug name; pypdf gave no x-coordinates for the digits). Formulary sig and quantity limits are as printed; the document prints no sig, so the sig is the label starting dose. Generic levothyroxine tablets are Tier 1 with no PA (PDG p. 68); the brand Synthroid is Tier 3, so the plan does not prefer the brand and boglActive is false. Not listed: Tirosint, Tirosint-SOL, Thyquidity, Ermeza, Unithroid, Euthyrox. Liothyronine and desiccated thyroid are in the next class. [Sonnet check 2026-11-06: tiers and flags re-read in layout (row-aligned) extraction, not flattened text; nonformulary reasons reworded to the front-matter wording; added Unithroid and Euthyrox as not listed.] [Reused: same national Humana PDP formulary] [Audit 2026-11-22: "TIROSINT (levothyroxine capsule)" is not on the printed Humana list; absence is not exclusion (the guide, p.7, says to ask Humana whether an unlisted drug is covered), matching the NY/CA/VA/IL Humana records] [Audit 2026-11-22: "TIROSINT-SOL (levothyroxine oral solution)" is not on the printed Humana list; absence is not exclusion (the guide, p.7, says to ask Humana whether an unlisted drug is covered), matching the NY/CA/VA/IL Humana records] [Audit 2026-11-22: "Thyquidity (levothyroxine oral solution)" is not on the printed Humana list; absence is not exclusion (the guide, p.7, says to ask Humana whether an unlisted drug is covered), matching the NY/CA/VA/IL Humana records] [Audit 2026-11-22: "Ermeza (levothyroxine oral solution)" is not on the printed Humana list; absence is not exclusion (the guide, p.7, says to ask Humana whether an unlisted drug is covered), matching the NY/CA/VA/IL Humana records] [Audit 2026-11-22: "Unithroid (levothyroxine tablet)" is not on the printed Humana list; absence is not exclusion (the guide, p.7, says to ask Humana whether an unlisted drug is covered), matching the NY/CA/VA/IL Humana records] [Audit 2026-11-22: "Euthyrox (levothyroxine tablet)" is not on the printed Humana list; absence is not exclusion (the guide, p.7, says to ask Humana whether an unlisted drug is covered), matching the NY/CA/VA/IL Humana records]
